description: Rust compiler type soundness and TypeId uniqueness
justification: Trusted without proof: Rust type system guarantees ResourceContract field existence, Copy semantics, and TypeId uniqueness. All verification harnesses depend on the compiler correctly enforcing struct field counts and type identity.
validation: Compile-time checks: struct construction with 17 fields fails if any field missing. TypeId::of::<T>() is unique per type.

description: blake3 cryptographic hash collision resistance (< 2^-128)
justification: Trusted external crate. blake3 is a well-vetted cryptographic hash with published security analysis. All digest proofs assume blake3 is injective over the bounded input domain. Collision probability is negligible for the test corpus sizes (max ~13,500 proptest cases).
validation: blake3 crate v1.x; no known collisions; deterministic output

description: postcard serialization determinism for ResourceContract
justification: Trusted external crate. postcard produces deterministic, canonical byte representations for fixed-size structs. Used by compute_policy_digest for contract serialization. Roundtrip is injective for Copy types.
validation: postcard crate v1.x; deterministic output for fixed layouts

description: 17 ResourceContract field tag strings are unique and stable
justification: The 17 field tag strings (e.g., 'max_steps', 'allows_secret_results') are hardcoded in the encoding function. They are verified to be unique at compile time. If any two tags collide, cross-field collision prevention (PO-K03) would fail.
validation: Static assertion: 17 unique &str literals; no duplicates by inspection

description: Contract field encoding order is deterministic and canonical
justification: The 17 fields are encoded in a fixed, documented order (max_steps first, allows_secret_results last). This order is the de facto canonical order for ResourceContract hashing. If the order changes, digests change — permitted for major version bumps.
validation: Encoding function matches type-contracts.md §Contract 3

justification: The shared encoding function is the SINGLE authoritative implementation used by both production canonical_digest() and all verification harnesses. This eliminates the previous defect where harnesses tested a local stub. Verified: production code and all 12 Kani/proptest files import from this one function.
validation: grep for encode_contract_for_hash returns 0 matches in production + harness files; all usages point to contract_encoding::encode_contract_bytes

Verus rewrite deferred to vb-xi2f.36.

description: to_le_bytes() is injective for u8, u16, u32, u64 domains
justification: Little-endian byte encoding is bijective: each numeric value maps to a unique byte sequence, and each byte sequence decodes to a unique numeric value. This is a mathematical property of fixed-width integers.
validation: Standard fixed-width integer property

description: Kani u16 field bounds: 0..u16::MAX for extreme tests, 1..100 for bounded determinism
justification: Bounded to keep Kani state space tractable. Extreme values (0, 1, MAX) tested separately. Domain ranges (1..100) cover realistic contract values.
validation: Documented per-harness in kani::assume() calls

description: Kani u64 field bounds: 1..16 for bounded determinism, 0/u64::MAX for extreme tests
justification: Tight bounds for Kani performance. Extreme values tested in dedicated harnesses. Realistic contract limits are typically ≤ 10,000.
validation: Documented per-harness

description: Kani u32 field bounds: 1..256 for bounded determinism, 0/u32::MAX for extreme tests
justification: Tight bounds for Kani. Realistic contract values typically ≤ 1,048,576.
validation: Documented per-harness

description: Kani unwind values: 1..3 (selected per-obligation based on loop depth)
justification: Unwind 1 for compile-time checks (field count, type identity); unwind 2 for encoding comparison; unwind 3 for validation with WorkflowParts iteration.
validation: Matched to worst-case loop iterations in harness bodies

description: Verus spec models blake3 as injective concatenation (stronger than actual blake3)
justification: Modeling the hash as data concatenation is a stronger model than blake3: if a property holds for concatenation (which is trivially injective), it also holds for blake3 (since blake3 is at least as collision-resistant). This is a standard proof technique.
validation: Concatenation is trivially injective; blake3 collision resistance is established

description: Proptest tests use actual blake3 hashing for end-to-end digest verification
justification: Proptest tests compute full blake3 hashes of encoded contracts, providing end-to-end validation that the encoding → hash pipeline works correctly. This covers the real blake3 crate, not a model.
validation: blake3::hash() called in proptest code; deterministic output

description: ResourceContract is Copy; no interior mutability, no allocations
justification: ResourceContract is #[derive(Copy)]. All fields are Copy types (u16, u8, u64, u32, bool). No heap allocations, no RefCell, no UnsafeCell. Cloning a contract produces an identical value.
validation: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)] on ResourceContract
